Target and actual: reading the gap

Actual below target when starting or under load — P0087, pressure too low. Look at the supply: fuel in the tank, air in the system, a clogged filter, the lift pump, the high-pressure pump, injectors leaking into the return. A Mercedes Sprinter stalled when it was running out of fuel: a low rail pressure code was stored, and after a few cranks the fuel was drawn through and the engine started (details on the blog: “Mercedes Sprinter stalled and won’t start”).

No pressure at all — check the high-pressure pump and its valves. On a 2012 MAN TGX the pump delivered no fuel: its pressure relief valve was stuck open; after it was restored and the system bled, the engine started (details on the blog: “MAN TGX 2012 wouldn’t start — the high-pressure pump wasn’t pumping”).

Actual above target or jumping — P0088, pressure too high: the metering valve, the regulator, the sensor or their wiring. Check the sensor’s 5 V supply and ground and look at its signal with an oscilloscope.

Target and actual match, but the engine smokes — pressure isn’t the problem, look at the injectors and air. On an excavator with a Cummins engine, target and actual matched, but black smoke and imbalance remained — the advice was to have the injectors checked by fuel injection specialists (details on the blog: “Excavator with a Cummins engine — black smoke”).

Where the electrician’s job ends

An electrician with a scan tool finds the direction: data, codes, wiring, connectors, sensors, power to the valves. Wiring and connectors are the electrician’s to fix: on a 2018 bus, misfiring and loss of power came from a damaged terminal in an injector connector — after repinning, the SPN 653 code went away (details on the blog: “Bus diagnostics, 2018 — fixing SPN 653”). But bench-testing injectors, measuring return flow — how much fuel an injector leaks back — repairing the high-pressure pump and measuring compression are jobs for a fuel injection specialist and an engine mechanic. As in the lesson “Compression and mechanicals: when the electrics aren’t to blame”: write down your measurements honestly and pass the vehicle on.

Rail pressure is hundreds to thousands of bar. Don’t loosen high-pressure lines or the sensor with the engine running or right after it stops: wait for the pressure to drop — the time is in the manual. A jet of fuel at this pressure goes through skin — a serious injury, see a doctor at once. Look for leaks with your eyes and a piece of cardboard, never your hand; no smoking nearby.
SCR and AdBlue: repair, not an emulator

Components: the AdBlue tank with level, temperature and often quality sensors, tank and line heaters, the pump, the dosing injector in the exhaust pipe, the SCR catalyst, NOx sensors before and after it, and exhaust temperature sensors.

The main check is the NOx sensors. On a warm, healthy SCR, NOx after the catalyst is several times lower than before it: for example, 300 ppm before and about 30 after — roughly 90 %. If “after” is almost equal to “before”, the SCR isn’t working (P20EE; on trucks under J1939 — SPN 4364). NOx sensors start measuring once they’re warm: zeros on a cold engine aren’t a fault.

Fluid quality: AdBlue is a 32.5 % urea solution (tolerance 31.8–33.2 %), checked with a refractometer. Diluted fluid causes quality and efficiency codes. A 2022 DAF XF 106 had an active low AdBlue concentration code and a 20 km/h limit; after a reset the limit was lifted, but the concentration still has to be checked or the code will come back (details on the blog: “DAF XF 106 2022 — 20 km/h limit, AdBlue codes”).

A healthy SCR removes most of the NOx: the “after” sensor reads several times lower than the “before” one.

Scan tool tests: pump pressure (P20E8 — AdBlue pressure too low), a dosing test into a measuring container — the volume is compared with the target — and a heater test. White crystals on the dosing injector and in the pipe are a sign of poor spray or poor fluid.

Winter: AdBlue freezes at about −11 °C, which is why there are heaters. A heater fault means power, relay, fuse, connector and the heater’s resistance per the manufacturer’s data. After the engine stops, many trucks need time for the pump to empty AdBlue from the lines: don’t turn off the battery master switch right away, wait the time given in the vehicle’s manual — often about 80 seconds.

Not everything is complicated: on a 2025 Sinotruk the AdBlue warning was due to a low level — after topping up it went away (details on the blog: “Sinotruk 2025 — computer diagnostics”). For more on the fluid itself, see the app’s “AdBlue” section.

We don’t fit AdBlue emulators or “disable” SCR, EGR or the DPF in software — why is explained in the lessons “Adaptations and resets” and “Trucks and heavy equipment: a 24 V scan tool”. Explain it simply to the customer: a code is a signal about a specific fault that can be found — a NOx sensor, the pump, a heater, the dosing injector, wiring or bad fluid. An emulator doesn’t fix it, it hides it; without SCR there are several times more nitrogen oxides in the exhaust, and the vehicle no longer meets its emissions class. Finding the cause is often cheaper than it seems: top up or replace the fluid, repair a connector, replace one sensor.
If a truck has an AdBlue heater fault, I check the heater fuses and relays first, and only then the heaters themselves and the pump.

Wiring, connectors and sensors are the electrician’s job; bench-testing injectors, return flow and the high-pressure pump belong to a fuel injection specialist.

The driver lesson “Why the car won’t start” gives four steps you can do by ear and by eye. A technician needs more: every step needs a measurement with a number that says “OK” or “not OK”, and only then comes the next step. Start by asking what happens when the key is turned — silence, a click, slow or brisk cranking, “catches and dies” — and whether the dash lights up. The general method is in the lesson “Troubleshooting method and working with ECUs”; here it is applied to one complaint. On the phone I always start with the fuses. Then it depends on the symptom. A click but no cranking — a few firm taps with a hammer on the starter housing. An automatic that won’t crank in P — have them try N, with the brake pressed and the parking brake on. A silent fuel pump — a light tap on the bottom of the tank. If the car then starts, the part is worn: the starter, the range sensor or the pump needs checking and repair before it fails for good. On site, I still go step by step with measurements.
Steps 1–2. Battery, grounds and starter
Battery at rest — the car has sat, everything off: 12.4–12.9 V. Lower — charge and test it first, as in the lesson “Batteries for pros”: with a flat battery the other measurements tell you nothing.

Sag while cranking: probes on the battery posts — no lower than about 9.6 V. From the blog: a Kia Optima showed about 10 V with the ignition on and 7 V when cranking; on a Hyundai Bayon 2023 the starter wouldn’t crank and the interior lights didn’t dim, yet the battery sagged to 9 V. Both owners were advised to replace the battery: “the lights don’t dim” is no substitute for a measurement.

Losses under load, while cranking: from the battery “+” post to starter terminal 30 — up to 0.5 V; from the starter housing to the battery “−” post — up to 0.2–0.3 V. More than that — look for a corroded clamp, ground strap or cable.

Silence with a charged battery — the interlocks: automatic selector in P or N, clutch pedal fully down, brake pressed on push-button cars. Then the starter fuse and relay, and the positive at terminal 50 while cranking — almost the same as at the battery. From the blog: a Nissan X-Trail 2021 wouldn’t crank when cold — the starter relay under the left headlight was to blame.

There’s a positive at 50, but the starter clicks or cranks slowly — the problem is the starter itself (the solenoid and its contact discs, the brushes) or the power circuit. Cranking current — with a clamp meter: usually around 100–200 A for gasoline passenger cars. High current and slow — mechanical; low current and slow — resistance in the circuit. Details are in the lesson “Starter motor: design and testing”.
Steps 3–4. Cranking speed, shaft sensors and the immobilizer

If the starter cranks briskly, connect the scan tool and watch engine speed in live data while cranking: usually about 150–250 rpm. Zero while the starter turns — the ECU doesn’t see the crankshaft signal and gives neither injection nor spark; P0335, crankshaft position sensor circuit, is often stored.

P0340 — camshaft sensor circuit: depending on the system, the engine takes longer to start or doesn’t start at all. Shaft sensor signals are checked with an oscilloscope while cranking — see the lesson “Oscilloscope: seeing the signal”.

Shaft sensor codes may be left over from earlier glitches: record them, clear them and crank again — did they come back? From the blog: a Kia Soul 2009 had P0343 and P0336; after clearing they didn’t return, and the real reason it wouldn’t start was the fuel pump — it was getting power but not running.

Immobilizer: the key or lock symbol flashes; the engine doesn’t catch, or catches and dies after 1–2 seconds; the ECU has an immobilizer code or no communication with the immobilizer module. Then follow the lesson “Immobilizers & keys”: battery, spare key, interference on the key ring, fuses, power and ground of the module and antenna. We never disable or bypass the immobilizer, and we program keys only with the vehicle’s documents.

The dash stays dark or the scan tool can’t see the engine ECU — check power: fuses, ignition switch, main relay, ECU grounds (lesson “Fuel injection, ECU power and grounds”). From the blog: on a Lexus GS300 the instrument panel stayed dark with the ignition on, the starter cranked but the engine wouldn’t start — a faulty ignition switch contact group wasn’t passing power to some of the systems.

Step 5. Fuel

First the obvious — is there fuel in the tank? Then the prime: on many cars the pump runs for 2–3 seconds when the ignition is switched on and stops if the ECU sees no rotation. Not on all of them, though: on the Toyota Corolla 2014 from the blog the pump only comes on while cranking — silence with the ignition on is normal there. That car wouldn’t start because of a defective new fuel filter: there was no pressure.

If the pump is silent — fuse and relay, then the positive and ground at the pump connector under load, and the current with a clamp meter. From the blog: on a Nissan Patrol 2015 the fuse, relay and alarm cut-off were fine and voltage reached the pump module, but the positive contact in the module itself and the mating connector had burned.

Pressure — with a gauge on the fuel rail test port or through an adapter in the line. Multipoint (port) injection engines usually run about 2.5–4.5 bar (35–65 psi); the exact spec is in the manual. After shutdown the pressure should hold for a while; if it drops quickly, look for a leak: the pump check valve, the pressure regulator, an injector. With direct injection, rail pressure after the high-pressure pump is tens of bar even while cranking: read it with the scan tool — a low-pressure gauge doesn’t go there.

From the blog: a Toyota Hiace 2018 had code P1200 — per the scan tool’s description, the fuel pump control circuit or its relay. The code was cleared and didn’t return; voltage was reaching the pump, yet the pump only started after a light knock on the fuel module cover. Conclusion: replace the pump and check the module contacts.
Steps 6–7. Injector pulse and spark

Injector pulse — while cranking, with a dedicated injector noid light plugged into the harness connector in place of the injector, or with an oscilloscope. Don’t connect an ordinary test lamp to ECU pins or sensor circuits — as in the lesson “Fuel injection, ECU power and grounds”.

While cranking, the scan tool shows injection pulse width — that’s the ECU’s command, not proof the injector opened. No pulse on any injector — main relay, ECU power and grounds, crankshaft signal, immobilizer; none on one injector — its wire and its ECU pin.

Spark — only with a spark tester: put the removed coil or the plug wire on the tester, clip the tester to engine ground, crank briefly. A steady spark across the gap on every cylinder means the ignition works. Disable the injectors or the pump as the manual describes while you test, so fuel doesn’t flood the cylinders.

No spark on any coil — crankshaft sensor, ECU power and grounds, the coil fuse, immobilizer. From the blog: a Honda CR-V 1998 had no spark because of the igniter; the owner replaced it himself and mounted it on the distributor housing incorrectly — the ECU output transistor was damaged and the ECU had to be repaired.

Crank for no more than 10 seconds at a time, with 30–60 second pauses, and never bridge terminals 30 and 50 with a screwdriver: that bypasses the interlocks, and a car in gear will drive off. The fuel line is under pressure: relieve it as the manual describes, keep a fire extinguisher at hand, no sparks or flames. Don’t test for spark “to ground” or hold a lead in your hand: the secondary circuit carries tens of thousands of volts. Keep your hands and test leads away from the belts and the fan — the engine may start.
Step 8. When it’s mechanical

The starter cranks briskly, the scan tool shows engine speed, the key is recognized, pressure is in spec, there are injector pulses and spark — and the engine still won’t catch: check the mechanicals. Clues: an uneven cranking sound, cranking that’s too easy, camshaft/crankshaft correlation codes. Relative compression and timing with a scan tool — lesson “Engine tests with a scan tool: compression, balance, misfires, timing”; a compression gauge test — lesson “Compression and mechanicals: when the electrics aren’t to blame”. If it’s confirmed, tell the customer honestly and hand the car to an engine mechanic: you can’t fix mechanical faults with electrics.

Fog lights, roof-mounted light bars, auxiliary headlights, work lights on a truck — common jobs for an auto electrician and a common reason for calls after a “garage” install. From the blog: fog lights are very often wired straight through the switch, with no relay and no fuse — the wiring melts, contacts overheat, switches burn out. Simple rules for owners are in the drivers’ course lesson “Dashcam, head unit, lights: wiring them right,” how a relay works is in “Relays and control circuits,” and connections are in “Wiring and connector repair.” This lesson is the technician’s job: the diagram, the calculation and the routing, after which nothing overheats or chafes.
The diagram: power circuit and control circuit

Power circuit: battery positive → fuse right at the terminal → relay terminal 30 → terminal 87 → lights wired in parallel → ground. The wire is sized by the calculation below and kept as short as possible.

Control circuit: the cabin switch only energizes the relay coil — positive to 86 through the switch, 85 to ground. The coil draws a fraction of an amp, so the switch and its thin wire don’t heat up. A relay with a diode is polarized — as in the lesson “Relays and control circuits.”

Positive to the switch: for fog lights, from the parking light circuit, because under the Kazakhstan Traffic Rules they come on only with the parking lights on. Auxiliary high beams and a light bar are best controlled from the high-beam circuit: switch to low beam for an oncoming car, and they go off too.
An illuminated switch: the backlight comes from the instrument lighting or parking light circuit, and the indicator shows the driver the lights are on.
Ground is a separate wire of the same gauge as the positive, with a ring terminal to clean metal under a factory bolt or to the battery negative. A bad ground means dim light and flicker.
The relay has contacts rated with a margin and is mounted in a dry spot; the fuse holder is sealed, with a cover.

The calculation: current, fuse, wire, voltage drop

Current: I = P / U; calculate at 12 V — that builds in a margin. Two 55 W fog lights: 110 / 12 ≈ 9 A. A 180 W light bar: 180 / 12 = 15 A. The advertised power of cheap products often doesn’t match the real one — measure the current with a DC clamp meter and calculate from the reading.

The fuse protects the wire: the rating is about 1.25 times the working current, rounded up to a standard value, and no more than the wire can carry. For a pair of fog lights — 15 A, for a 15 A light bar — 20 A.

Gauge is chosen by the fuse and the length; the table is in the lesson “Dashcam, head unit, lights.” For fog lights on a 15 A fuse — 2.5 mm², for a light bar on 20 A — 4 mm². The wire is stranded copper, not copper-clad aluminum (CCA).

Check by voltage drop: copper wire resistance R = 0.0175 × L / S (Ω; L is the length in meters, S the cross-section in mm²), drop ΔU = I × R. A pair of fog lights, 9 A, 5 m positive wire: 1.5 mm² — 0.53 V, 2.5 mm² — 0.32 V. A light bar, 15 A, 5 m of 4 mm² wire — about 0.33 V. The target, as in the lesson “Electricity in the car”: up to 0.5 V on the positive side and up to 0.2–0.3 V on ground. If the ground runs as a wire back to the battery, calculate it too.
A halogen bulb is very sensitive to voltage: every half volt lost noticeably reduces the light, and a wire at its limit also heats up.

Inrush current: a cold halogen filament draws several times its working current for the first fraction of a second, and LED light bars and LED headlights have capacitors at the driver input — a short current surge at switch-on. So the relay gets contacts rated with a margin, connections are crimped, and the fuse is sized by calculation, not cut to the bone. If it blows at switch-on with no short, measure the real current with a clamp meter.

I never wire high-power lights straight through the switch: only a relay and a fuse near the battery, and I don’t skimp on the wiring. I use a quality fuse — a cheap one of unknown make may not blow at its rating but melt along with its holder. And if both fog lights later go out at once, I check the fuse, the relay and the power feed first; if only one is out, it’s almost always the bulb or a contact.
Routing: tape, split loom, rubber grommets
Before you start, disconnect the battery negative terminal. Route along the factory harnesses: there the wire is already protected from heat and movement, just like the factory one.

The wire goes in tape and in split loom. Tape depends on the location: cloth tape in the cabin, since it doesn’t squeak or rattle; PVC under the hood, since it isn’t bothered by moisture. Tape bundles and protects the harness but doesn’t insulate a joint — joints get heat shrink, as in the lesson “Wiring and connector repair.”

Split loom runs the full length under the hood, under the floor and anywhere the wire could rub; under the hood it’s heat-resistant and sized with room to spare. Secure the loom too and tape its ends: loose loom chafes the wire itself and collects dirt.

Through metal — only through rubber grommets. The factory firewall grommet is best: you pierce the rubber, not the metal. If you drill, first check what’s behind the panel, then deburr the hole, paint the edge against rust, and fit a grommet of the right size plus sealant. Without a grommet, vibration lets the edge cut through the loom and insulation down to the copper — a short to ground and a fire risk.

Secure it with zip ties to the factory harnesses, usually every 20–30 cm, so the wire doesn’t flop around. Don’t tie it to fuel or brake lines; keep it away from the exhaust manifold, turbo and other hot parts, and from the belt, fan, steering shaft and suspension. Where parts move — doors, hood, a truck’s tilt cab — leave a service loop with slack, in loom.
Under the hood and outside: sealed connectors with a seal on every wire and adhesive-lined heat shrink; mount the relay terminals down so water doesn’t sit in the socket.

From the blog: on a 2023 KamAZ, the wires were pinched during an earlier heater fan replacement, and vibration wore through the insulation — a short to ground, and the heater fuse kept blowing. On a 2023 Fendt combine, a control wire chafed against its protective loom — an open circuit; it was repaired with solder and heat shrink, laid back in loom and secured with ties so it wouldn’t chafe again.

A chafed positive wire shorts to the body. If the fuse sits at the lights or there’s no fuse at all, the whole wire from the battery burns — that’s a fire. So the fuse goes right at the terminal, rated for the wire. If it blows, look for the short; never fit a “bigger” fuse or a jumper in its place. Work with the battery negative disconnected, and drill only after making sure there are no wires, lines or tank behind the panel.
Lighting modules, CAN and LED interference

If the lights are switched by the body control module or a lighting module (the lesson “Module-controlled and CAN lighting”), you never splice into the CAN bus — not for power, not for a “signal”: codes will appear and the car may not start. Don’t load module outputs with extra lights either: an output is designed for its own bulb, monitors its current, and on overload it shuts off or burns out. Auxiliary lights go only through their own relay fed from the battery.

On these cars the parking light wire often comes from a PWM module output — check it with an oscilloscope. On PWM the relay coil may chatter, and the module may log a code. Then look for the factory provision: many cars have a fog light connector in the harness, and the function is enabled with a scan tool — per the service manual.

From the blog: on a Toyota Highlander, the right turn signal stayed on constantly and the hazard switch made no difference; after the installed alarm’s connectors were unplugged, the fault went away. Aftermarket equipment in the lighting circuits is the first thing to check.

Interference: an LED driver is a switching converter, and a cheap one without filtering is “noisy” — when the light bar comes on, the radio hisses or drops out. What helps: a product with a conformity mark (the letter E with a country number), a solid ground, wires kept away from the antenna cable, and ferrite rings on the power leads at the driver. If that doesn’t help, replace the product.

A 24 V truck: lights and light bars rated for 24 V or with a suitable supply range per their spec sheet, and a relay with a 24 V coil; at the same power the current is half, as in the lesson “Trucks: the 24 V system and the J1939 bus.”
What the rules in Kazakhstan allow

Kazakhstan Traffic Rules: fog lights are switched on with the parking lights on (clause 133). They’re used in poor visibility — on their own or with low or high beams — and in the dark on unlit roads together with low or high beams (clause 132).
Spotlights and search lights — only outside populated areas and with no oncoming traffic (clause 135). Rear fog lights are not wired to the brake lights (clause 136).

The list of defects that prohibit operating a vehicle: the number, type, color, placement and operating mode of exterior lights must match the vehicle’s design (chapter 3, clause 11); no red lights at the front, and no white at the rear except reverse lights and the license plate light (clause 16).

Installing equipment not provided for in the design that affects road safety is a modification (clause 46 of the list). According to a police explanation (2025), any change to the lighting system counts as a modification; without registering it, the fine is under Article 590, part 7 of the Administrative Offenses Code. Discuss a light bar or lights that the model wasn’t designed with before the job, and check the registration procedure with the police.

The rules are per Ministry of Internal Affairs order No. 534 of 30.06.2023 (the Traffic Rules and the Basic Provisions for Admitting Vehicles to Operation). Before the job, check the current wording at adilet.zan.kz.

Auxiliary lights go only through a relay: the switch energizes the coil (a fraction of an amp), the light current flows from the battery through a fuse right at the terminal; ground is a separate wire to clean metal.

Calculation: I = P / U, the fuse about 1.25 × I up to a standard value and matched to the wire, drop ΔU = I × 0.0175 × L / S — up to 0.5 V on the positive side. With LEDs, allow for inrush and check for interference.

Routing: the wire in tape (cloth in the cabin, PVC under the hood) and in split loom, through metal only via rubber grommets, zip-tied to the factory harnesses, away from hot and moving parts; sealed connectors and heat shrink under the hood.
On cars with a lighting module and CAN, don’t splice into the bus and don’t load module outputs. Fog lights come on with the parking lights, and unregistered auxiliary lighting is a modification.

Key-off current limits, waiting for the modules to sleep, connecting an ammeter without breaking the circuit and searching by fuse voltage drop were covered in the lesson “Parasitic draw: how to track it down”. This lesson is practice: how a car goes to sleep step by step, how to spot a module that stays awake, how to find and remove the draw quickly and how to prove to the customer that it’s gone.

My rule: once the car is asleep, the key-off current should ideally be 0.06 A (60 mA) or less. Any more and I look for the cause, even if the car still starts for now. On most passenger cars it’s 20–50 mA, as in the lesson “Parasitic draw”; if the manufacturer gives its own limit, I check against that. Do the math: 60 mA is about 1.4 Ah a day, and over two weeks parked about 20 Ah — a third of a 60 Ah battery.
How a car goes to sleep: current steps

Right after switching off and locking, the current is high — hundreds of milliamps or even amps: modules are still running, the ECU holds the main relay, lights are on, the cooling fan may keep running.
Then the current drops in steps: the lights go out, comfort and infotainment modules fall asleep, the bus goes quiet. Each step is a module or a group of modules going to sleep.

The last step is the key-off current: module memory, the clock, the key fob receiver, the alarm. That’s what you compare with the limit. How long to wait is in the manual: some cars need just a few minutes, others, according to Pico Technology, 30 minutes to 2 hours.

On a BMW, for example, most modules should be asleep within the first 16 minutes, and the system flags any module still awake at 20 minutes as a sleep-mode preventer (“Energy Management”, The Bimmer Pub, 2016).

Sleeping modules sometimes wake briefly on their own — to check the battery or check in (telematics, a GSM alarm). Short spikes between long pauses are normal if the current between them is within the limit.

What wakes the car and how to spot a module that stays awake
Doors, hood and trunk — their switches; buttons and the key fob; a keyless-entry key near the car — move it well away.
An alarm with sensors and a GSM module, factory telematics, remote start — they wake on a schedule or on command.
Bus traffic: one module sends a message and the rest wake up. A connected scan tool wakes the bus too, so leave the diagnostic port alone while the car sleeps.

A drain can be intermittent (see the blog: “Why the battery goes flat overnight”): the module doesn’t stay awake every time. Then log the current for hours — a scope with a clamp — or measure several times.

The main sign of a module that stays awake is a step: the current dropped but got stuck at a few hundred milliamps and stays there for hours. A light or a dash cam gives the same kind of step, so look at the bus: put a scope on CAN-H and CAN-L to ground, at the diagnostic port or at a module. In sleep, both high-speed CAN wires sit near zero — the transceivers bias the lines to ground (Texas Instruments TCAN1042 data sheet). About 2.5 V with frames running means some module is holding the bus awake. Fault-tolerant body CAN has different sleep levels — see the manual. Connect the scan tool afterwards: it will wake the bus, but it shows the codes, and on some cars the energy management module records what kept the network awake.

Searching without taking things apart: the clamp and fuse voltage drop
Put a DC clamp meter around the battery negative cable; if several wires leave the terminal, enclose them all. Warm the clamp up and zero it before measuring — Pico suggests waiting 10 minutes.

Then use the same clamp along the harnesses: the positive feeds to the fuse boxes, the harness to the trunk or a door, add-on equipment wiring. Current in a harness tells you right away which way to go, and the car doesn’t wake up.
Clamp feed wires only: if a harness carries both the positive and the ground of the same load, the currents cancel and the clamp reads almost zero.

Fuse voltage drop: a millivoltmeter with 0.1 mV resolution on the test points on top. Current = drop ÷ fuse resistance. Littelfuse mini fuses are typically 7.42 mΩ at 10 A, so 1 mV ≈ 135 mA, and 17.75 mΩ at 5 A, so 1 mV ≈ 56 mA. Other ratings are in the picture.
The whole 0.06 A limit across one 10 A fuse is only 0.45 mV. That’s why you need a sensitive meter and a table from the maker of those particular fuses: other brands have different resistance.

If the fuses show nothing but the clamp on the negative still shows a drain, move to the heavy cables that have no fuse or one fuse for everything: alternator B+, the starter positive, high-current fusible links, amplifier and inverter cables run straight from the battery. Clamp B+ with the engine off: current there points to a shorted rectifier diode or the regulator, provided nothing else is fed from that cable (check the diagram). How to disconnect the alternator for the check is in the lesson “Parasitic draw”. A case from practice — a 2020 Hyundai Santa Fe (details in the blog: “Hyundai Santa Fe 2020 — excessive current draw”): the drain was about 14 A; after checking the charging system and the circuits and disconnecting modules one by one, the culprit turned out to be the alternator with an internal fault. It was replaced, and the follow-up measurement was normal.
Common culprits and how to fix them

Add-on equipment — an alarm, dash cam, amplifier, GPS tracker — wired to constant power or not shutting off. Fix: power it from the ignition (ACC or 15) through a fuse tap in a non-critical circuit, heavy loads through a relay switched by the ignition; for a dash cam with parking mode, a low-voltage cutoff per its instructions. How to wire it is in the course “For drivers”, lesson “Dashcam, head unit, lights: wiring them in properly”.
A stuck relay: a heater, pump or fan keeps running after shutdown. Fix: replace the relay with one of the same circuit and find out why it stuck — as in the lesson “Relays and control circuits”.
An alternator with a shorted diode — current through B+ with the engine off. Fix: repair or replace the alternator, then check charging.

Water in a connector or module: the module won’t sleep or “sees” a button as pressed. Fix: find where the water gets in (drains, seals), dry it out, clean the contacts, replace corroded terminals — as in the lesson “Wiring and connector repair”.

A module that stays awake for no visible reason: check its power, ground, inputs (switches) and codes. If the manufacturer has released a software update for it, install it only through official channels — the dealer or J2534 with official access, as in the lesson “Official reprogramming” of the course “Scan tool diagnostics”.
Trunk, glove box and underhood lights: the switch is broken or isn’t pressed, so the light stays on with the lid closed. Fix: adjust or replace the switch.

From practice (in the blog: “Finding a hidden current draw”): a faulty amplifier after an audio install — a constant 0.2 A drain; corroded alarm wires — the alarm didn’t fully cut power and the battery went flat in 2–3 days; an old power-window module — 0.1 A while switched off.
Checking after the repair and a record for the customer
Reassemble everything you took apart, close the doors and hood or latch the locks as for the first measurement; move the key away.
Let the car fall asleep again — at least as long as the first time — and measure the same way: same clamp, same cable.
0.06 A or less, or the manual’s limit — done. More than that — keep looking: there can be two culprits.
Check the battery and charging: after a deep discharge the battery may need replacing, and the alternator must stay in spec under load — as in the lesson “Charging system”.
Write it down for the customer: current before and after, how many minutes after locking you measured, what you found and what you did. If they come back, you’ll have something to compare with.

That’s how it was done on a Lexus LX 570 (details in the blog: “Lexus LX 570 — battery replacement, parasitic draw and alternator check”). The battery had been discharged to about 3 V. The terminals were cleaned and a new battery fitted — and the job didn’t stop there: once the modules were asleep the current was measured at 0.01 A (10 mA), and the alternator gave 14.1 V under load. A conclusion with numbers: no drain and no charging problem at the time of the check; the cause was the deeply discharged old battery.

While the ammeter is in series with the negative, don’t switch on the ignition, the lights or the starter. The alternator B+ cable and other heavy cables are always live at battery voltage: clamp only over the insulation, and disconnect wires only with the negative off. Never put jumpers in place of fuses, and never take power for add-on equipment from the airbag, ABS, engine ECU or fuel pump circuits.
Oleg’s limit: 0.06 A or less once the modules are asleep; more than that — find the cause. The exact limit is in the manual.
A car falls asleep in steps. Current stuck on a step plus about 2.5 V and frames on CAN means a module hasn’t gone to sleep. A scan tool wakes the bus — connect it afterwards.

Search without taking things apart: clamp on the negative and along the harnesses, then fuse voltage drop — current = mV ÷ resistance. Nothing there — check alternator B+, the starter and heavy cables.
Once the cause is fixed, let the car sleep again, measure the same way and record the before-and-after current for the customer.

A sole proprietor on the simplified regime doesn’t have to hire a bookkeeper or keep full accounting books until income reaches a threshold. But “keeping nothing” isn’t an option either: documents for every job, income records, the tax return and payments are on you. This course shows how to handle all of it yourself, using an auto electrician’s repair shop in Almaty as the example.
Information based on Kazakhstan law as of October 26, 2026. This is not legal or tax advice: rules change — check kgd.gov.kz and the Tax Code, or ask your local tax office (UGD).
This course is for your own IP

This course teaches you to keep the books of your own IP. On the simplified regime you can’t keep books for others for a fee: “Accounting or audit activities” (OKED 69201, 69202, 69205) is item 23 of the list of activities barred from the simplified regime (Government Resolution No. 970 of November 14, 2025). Tax consulting (OKED 69203) is item 22 of the same list.
What you must keep
Source documents — prepare and keep them: a contract or work order, a certificate of completed work (act), waybills for parts, fiscal receipts, and e-invoices (ESF) if you issued any.
Tax records — keep tax registers: they show where the income in your return came from.
Inventory counts — do them: compare what your documents show with what you actually have, such as parts on the shelf.
Form 910.00 — file it for every half-year; payments for yourself — make them every month (deadlines are in lesson 2).
E-invoices (ESF) — since 2026, simplified-regime businesses must issue them too; a sale with a cash register (KKM) receipt needs no ESF (details in lesson 10).

An IP on the simplified regime may skip accounting books and financial statements if all of these hold: annual income is at most 135,000 MCI (₸583,875,000 in 2026), the IP isn’t registered for VAT, and it isn’t a natural monopoly. The basis is the Law “On Accounting and Financial Reporting” (Art. 2(2)(1)) and Art. 202(4) of the Tax Code; the State Revenue Committee (KGD) explains it the same way. Simplified-regime taxpayers aren’t registered for VAT (Art. 99 of the Tax Code), so for a repair shop the key condition is income.

If income since the start of the year goes over the threshold, accounting books are kept from the month after the month it was crossed. For a small shop that’s far off: at ₸4,000,000 a month, the year comes to ₸48,000,000 — about 8% of the threshold.
What to keep records in
Whatever you choose, one rule applies: every amount in your records is backed by a document, and the records add up to your return. Here’s what IPs use:
The ISNA taxpayer account — you file returns and notices there with your digital signature (EDS) (details in lesson 4).
E-Salyq Business — the KGD mobile app. According to accounting websites citing the KGD, it offers income tracking, receipts and Form 910.00 filing — check with your local tax office.
Bank apps — for example, Kaspi has a “Taxes” section for paying taxes and contributions (per the Kaspi Guide).
Your own spreadsheet or 1C — for income entries and a list of documents.

A simplified-regime IP has three rhythms of deadlines: monthly payments, Form 910.00 and its tax every half-year, and Form 200.00 every quarter if you have employees. The dates below follow the KGD tax calendar for 2026. It’s handy to enter them once in your phone calendar with reminders.

The deadlines here are for the simplified regime. Anyone who was on the simplified regime in 2025 and didn’t file the notice of the applied tax regime between January 1 and March 1, 2026 was moved to the general regime (OUR) from January 1, 2026 — with different forms and deadlines. Check your regime in your taxpayer account.
Every month — by the 25th

Payments for yourself — mandatory pension contributions (OPV), employer pension contributions (OPVR), social contributions (SO) and health insurance contributions (VOSMS) — and, if you have employees, personal income tax (IPN) and payroll contributions are paid monthly, no later than the 25th of the following month. For October 2026 — by November 25, for November — by December 25, for December — by January 25, 2027.

On the simplified regime, tax is calculated from income, so the main thing in your records is not to miss a single receipt and not to report anything extra. Using an auto electrician’s shop in Almaty, let’s see what money counts as income for Form 910.00.
Income — with no deduction for expenses

On the simplified regime, the tax base is income for the half-year. Expenses — parts, bay rent, tools — aren’t deducted from it. Only adjustments reduce income: a refund to a customer, a discount, a price change. That’s what Article 724 of the Tax Code says; we checked its text against a copy of the code in open sources — confirm the details with your local tax office.

Tax = income × rate. The base rate is 4%, and the local maslikhat (council) can change it. For Almaty, accounting websites report a 3% rate for 2026 (maslikhat decision No. 256 of November 28, 2025); we haven’t checked the text of the decision — confirm the rate with your local tax office.
What goes into income
Cash for repairs and diagnostics — with a fiscal receipt from the cash register (KKM).
Card and QR payments (Kaspi Pay and others) — income too, and also with a fiscal receipt.
Transfers from companies and IPs — fleets, businesses — to the IP account under an invoice and act; you issue ESFs for them.
Money for work sent to the mechanic’s personal card is IP income too. Taking payment this way is a risk (see below).

About the register: according to clarifications in open sources (accounting websites, 2025–2026), a fiscal receipt is needed for cash, card and QR payments, and a Kaspi bank receipt doesn’t count as fiscal; a transfer from a company’s bank account under an invoice usually doesn’t require a KKM receipt. Refunds and prepayments

An IP files returns, notices, and applications with the tax office electronically and signs them with their own EDS. The main place for this is the ISNA taxpayer account. Let’s see what to look for there and how to check once a month that you owe nothing. The ISNA taxpayer account — returns, notices, applications. Per explanations in public sources, use the new account and stop using the old one.

Bank apps — per the KGD, you can file the tax regime notice through them; taxes can be paid, for example, in the Kaspi “Taxes” section.
On paper — at your local tax office (UGD).

In the account, notices and applications go through the “Submit documents” section. Per the KGD, that’s how the notice of the applied tax regime was filed: ISNA account → “Submit documents” → the notice you need → sign with your EDS. Your EDS is the key to the account

You sign in and sign documents with your own EDS. So never hand the key and password to “helpers,” and take the link to the account from the official kgd.gov.kz website, not from messages or ads.
Personal account: debt or overpayment

Your personal account is a reconciliation with the budget: for each tax you see how much was assessed, how much you paid, and what’s left. What’s left is the balance: zero means all paid, debt means you owe more, overpayment means you paid too much. Per finance.kz (2026), you open it in the ISNA account under “Services” → “Personal account,” and you can generate a statement there too. You can also check for debt with the KGD service “Information on the absence (presence) of debt.”

Per accounting portals, the ISNA system charges penya (late-payment interest) automatically for every day late (how it’s calculated is in lesson 7). The bigger the debt, the tougher the measures. Per mybuh.kz’s breakdown of the new Tax Code (March 18, 2026): a debt of up to 20 MCI (up to ₸86,500 in 2026) gets a debt notice; from 20 to 45 MCI (up to ₸194,625) — a formal notification, suspension of debit transactions on the account, and a collection order; over 45 MCI — an account freeze and an inventory of property. Besides the tax every half-year, a simplified-regime IP makes four payments for themselves every month: pension contributions OPV and OPVR, social contributions SO, and health insurance contributions VOSMS. The deadline is the 25th of the following month (lesson 2). Rates and amounts below are for 2026, with a minimum wage of ₸85,000.
Four payments and what they’re based on
OPV — 10% of declared income. The IP declares the income for the math themselves, from 1 to 50× minimum wage a month, so in 2026 the contribution runs from ₸8,500 to ₸425,000.
OPVR — 3.5% of the same declared income (it was 2.5% in 2025): from ₸2,975 to ₸148,750 a month.
SO — 5% of declared income minus OPV; the base is at least 1× and at most 7× minimum wage, so from ₸4,250 to ₸29,750.
VOSMS — 5% of 1.4× minimum wage (₸119,000), so ₸5,950 a month at any income.

A note on sources: the rates for OPV, OPVR, and VOSMS “for yourself” come from the Kaspi Guide and the accounting portal pro1c.kz, and figuring SO on income minus OPV comes from a State Social Insurance Fund (GFSS) clarification (the Social Code itself doesn’t say so directly). Before paying, check the amounts in your bank app or with your local tax office.

Example. An auto electrician declares ₸200,000 a month. OPV is ₸20,000, OPVR ₸7,000, SO (200,000 − 20,000) × 5% = ₸9,000, VOSMS ₸5,950. That’s ₸41,950 a month in total. At the minimum income of 1× minimum wage it would be ₸21,675.
A month with no income. Per the Kaspi Guide, you can skip OPV, OPVR, and SO for such a month, but VOSMS — ₸5,950 — is paid every month. Confirm this with your local tax office.
How to pay without mistakes
You pay through a bank app — for example, the “Taxes” section in Kaspi Pay (per the Kaspi Guide) — through the taxpayer account, or at a bank. Before paying, check four things:
IIN — your own, as in your IP registration.

Payment type: the KBK (budget classification code) and KNP (payment purpose code) show what it is — OPV, OPVR, SO, or VOSMS. In the app, check that the right payment is selected; if you enter the codes yourself, check them against your bank’s data or confirm with your local tax office.
Period — the month you’re paying for, not the month you pay in: October’s payment made in November is a payment for October.
Amount — as calculated for that month.

A simplified-regime IP files Form 910.00 for every half-year. The next one is for H2 2026: file by February 15, 2027, and pay the tax by February 25, 2027 (lesson 2). Let’s walk through filling it out using an auto electrician’s shop in Almaty.

The form number didn’t change in 2026 — it’s still 910.00. But per accounting portals, new reporting forms were approved by Ministry of Finance Order No. 695 of November 12, 2025, and they’re being updated in the account in stages. Filling it out step by step
Pull the half-year’s income from your records: KKM receipts plus transfers from businesses to your account, minus refunds.
Sign in to the ISNA account with your own EDS and open Form 910.00; per accounting portals, you can also file it in E-Salyq Business.

Pay the tax by the 25th of the same month.
Check your personal account: assessed and paid match, balance 0 (lesson 4).

Filing Form 910.00 is only half the job: you still have to pay its tax, and on time. Be even one day late and late-payment interest (penya) starts to accrue, while an unpaid debt eventually leads to restrictions on your bank account. Let’s see how to pay, where to check that the money arrived, and how the interest is calculated.
Payment deadline: the 25th

The Form 910.00 tax is paid no later than the 25th of the second month after the half-year — 10 days after the filing deadline. For H2 2026, by Feb 25, 2027; for H1 2027, by Aug 25, 2027 under the same rule (check the KGD calendar for 2027). Payments for yourself and your employees are separate: they’re due every month by the 25th (lesson 5).

How to pay and check
Take the amount from your Form 910.00: the tax is your half-year income times the rate (lesson 3).
You can pay in the taxpayer account or in a bank app — for example, Kaspi has a “Taxes” section (per the Kaspi Guide).
Check the payment details — the KBK (budget classification code) and KNP (payment purpose code) (lesson 5): a wrong code is a common reason for a “debt” when the tax seems to be paid.
Keep the payment receipt together with the return.

After paying, open your personal tax account (litsevoy schyot). According to accounting websites, it’s in the ISNA taxpayer account under “Services” → “Personal account” (details in lesson 4). For each tax it shows how much was assessed from your return, how much was paid, and the balance: a debt, zero, or an overpayment. Pay too much or pay twice and you’ll have an overpayment. How to offset or refund it isn’t covered in the official 2026 clarifications we checked — ask your local tax office.

Late-payment interest: how it’s calculated

Interest accrues on the unpaid amount for every day late — from the day after the payment deadline, including the day you pay. According to clarifications in open sources (mybuh.kz, 2026), the annual interest rate is 1.25 times the National Bank base rate, and ISNA accrues it automatically every day. The base rate changes, so check the current interest rate at kgd.gov.kz or with your local tax office. The lesson’s examples use a hypothetical rate of 0.05% per day, just to show how the math works.

Example. The Form 910.00 tax for H2 2026 is ₸180,000, due Feb 25, 2027, paid on Mar 5, 2027. Days late: Feb 26, 27, 28 and Mar 1 through 5 — 8 days. Interest at the hypothetical rate: 180,000 × 0.05% × 8 = ₸720. Pay on Feb 25, 2027 — no interest. Pay only part on time — interest runs on the unpaid remainder.

An unpaid debt won’t go away on its own. According to accounting websites (mybuh.kz, March 18, 2026), with a tax debt of up to 20 MCI you get a notification; from 20 to 45 MCI — a notice, suspension of debit transactions on the account, and a collection order; over 45 MCI — an account freeze and a property inventory. In 2026, 20 MCI is ₸86,500 and 45 MCI is ₸194,625.

Everyone makes mistakes on a return: you forget an act for a fleet, mix up an amount, or miss the Form 910.00 deadline. What matters is fixing them yourself, and as early as possible: that means less interest and fewer questions from the KGD. Let’s see how it’s done.
Found a mistake? File an amended return

If a filed Form 910.00 has a mistake or is missing income, you file an amended (additional) return for the same period — according to clarifications in open sources (digitalbusiness.kz, July 30, 2026), with the actual figures. You file it the same way as the regular one — for example, in the ISNA taxpayer account with your EDS (lesson 4). Missed income isn’t moved to the next half-year: it’s corrected in the return for the period it belongs to.

More income means more tax. Pay the difference right away: the half-year tax was due by the 25th of the second month after it, so interest on the extra amount runs from the day after that deadline (lesson 7). Example: a ₸400,000 act for a fleet was left off Form 910.00 for H1 2026. At a 3% rate (Almaty, lesson 3), the extra tax is ₸12,000, with interest from Aug 26, 2026 through the payment day.

Missed the deadline? The system files a zero return

If Form 910.00 isn’t filed on time, the ISNA system generates a zero return by itself — that’s how the KGD explains it. After that, the regular return can no longer be filed: the correct figures go only on an amended return. A zero Form 910.00 when you had real income is a mistake: the KKM receipts and transfers haven’t gone anywhere. On top of that, late filing brings administrative liability (lesson 2).

Desk audits and notices

The mistake may be found without you. According to accounting websites (mybuh.kz, 2026), since 2026 desk audits (cameral control) have been preventive in nature, and a tax risk management system is in place. If a notice about a discrepancy arrives in your taxpayer account, don’t put it off:
Read the notice: which period, what amount, and the response deadline.
Check it against your documents: KKM receipts, acts, transfers from companies, e-invoices (ESF).
If the mistake is confirmed, file an amended Form 910.00 and pay the extra tax and interest.
If there’s no mistake, respond by the deadline in the notice and attach documents; ask your local tax office exactly how.

Old mistakes need fixing too. Per the text of Art. 65 of the Tax Code (a copy of the code in open sources), the statute of limitations for taxes is 3 years after the end of the tax period, and 5 years for large taxpayers and some others: during all that time the KGD can review the return and assess additional tax. The sooner you fix a mistake yourself, the less interest builds up.

Every job and every purchase at the shop must be backed by a document. An IP on the simplified regime, even without accounting books, must prepare and keep source documents (Art. 202(4) of the Tax Code, lesson 1). Your Form 910.00 income is calculated from them, and they’re also your protection if the KGD has questions.
What documents a shop has
Work order or estimate — what we’ll do, on which vehicle, and for how much; agree on it with the customer before work starts.
Fiscal cash register (KKM) receipt — for cash, card and QR payments, for the full amount paid (lesson 3).
Contract — with a fleet or company: what work, prices, and how payment works.
Certificate of completed work (act) — the work was handed over and accepted; both sides sign it.
E-invoice (ESF) — when a company or IP pays by bank transfer without a receipt: since 2026, simplified-regime businesses must issue them too (lesson 10).
Supplier’s waybill — for parts and materials; if the supplier issued an ESF, keep that too.

A fleet: a contract, a work order, an act signed by both sides, an ESF, and now and then a reconciliation statement. A supplier: a waybill for what you bought. Per the KGD, for a buyer on the general regime the date the service is received is the date the act is signed, so date the act by when the work was actually accepted.

Since 2026, simplified-regime businesses issue electronic invoices (ESFs) too. When you need an ESF and when a receipt is enough is covered in the course “IP for a repair shop” (the lesson on fleets and companies). Here’s the bookkeeper’s view: how to fill in an ESF without mistakes, what to check in incoming ESFs from suppliers, and how to keep a register so your ESFs match your acts, payments, and Form 910.00.
When an ESF is needed, in brief

Needed: since 2026, simplified-regime businesses must issue ESFs even though they don’t pay VAT (Art. 208(1) of the Tax Code, KGD clarification of Jan. 27, 2026). For a repair shop, that’s mainly work for a company or IP paid by transfer to your account under an act, with no receipt.

Not needed: for a sale with a KKM receipt, through a terminal or a special app (the buyer’s IIN goes on the receipt if they ask), and for a sale to an individual paying by card or e-money (Art. 208(2)).
The amount doesn’t matter: the “ESF for deals over 1,000 MCI” rule was removed from the code (KGD).
Virtual Warehouse goods and imported goods are a special case (Art. 208(3)); see lesson 11.
From the act to the ESF

An ESF is issued in the ESF information system and signed with the IP’s EDS. It holds no new data: everything comes from the signed act of completed work. The supplier is you, with your IIN; the recipient is the company, with its BIN as in the contract and act; the work and amount are as in the act.

VAT. Simplified-regime taxpayers don’t register for VAT (Art. 99 of the Tax Code, KGD clarification), so no VAT is shown on the ESF: the ESF amount equals the act amount.

Date. Per the KGD, for a buyer on the general regime the date the service is received is the date the act is signed; issue the ESF right after signing. The ESF deadline for simplified-regime businesses isn’t stated in the official sources we checked — confirm it with the KGD.
Incoming ESFs from suppliers

When you buy parts by bank transfer, it’s the supplier who issues the ESF — to you — and it shows up in the ESF system. For your books it’s a purchase check: match the ESF against the waybill — same supplier, same goods, quantity, and amount (as in the parts lesson of the course “IP for a repair shop”). An incoming ESF doesn’t reduce income: on the simplified regime, tax is figured on income with no deduction for expenses (lesson 3).
Register: act, ESF, payment

So no ESF gets lost, keep a simple register of work for companies: act number and date, client, amount, ESF number, payment date and amount. Once a month, check it against the ESF system and your bank statement: every act without a receipt has its own ESF for the same amount, and every payment from a company is in income for Form 910.00 (lesson 3). An act with no payment is the client’s debt — confirm it with a reconciliation statement.

The Virtual Warehouse

The Virtual Warehouse (VW) is the part of the ESF system that tracks the movement of goods on a separate Ministry of Finance list. Whether it affects a repair shop depends on what you buy and sell: oil, fluids, batteries, parts. Let’s see how to check that and what changes in your documents and records.
The list from 2026

From January 1, 2026, the VW list was updated by a Ministry of Finance order of Oct. 31, 2025; sources give the order number differently, No. 661 or No. 681. Per the accounting portal pro1c.kz (Nov. 12, 2025), the list added petroleum products of group 2710 — gasolines, fuel, fuel oil, and others — plus bitumen, propane and butane, and acids.

Tires (code 4011), batteries (8507), and vehicle parts (8708) aren’t among the added items. Whether they’re on the list as a whole isn’t confirmed in the sources we checked: compare by product code or confirm with the KGD. Per the portals, the goods traceability rules were approved by Ministry of Finance Order No. 623 of Oct. 24, 2025.

How to hire your first employee and what they cost the IP is covered in the course “IP for a repair shop.” Here’s the monthly calculation through a bookkeeper’s eyes: what to accrue, what to withhold, how much to pay out, what to pay on top, what limits the payments have, and how to pull it all into a payroll sheet. Amounts are for 2026: minimum wage ₸85,000, MCI ₸4,325; rates per the Kaspi Guide and clarifications from the ENPF and GFSS.
The order of the calculation

The monthly calculation always goes in the same order. Salary is accrued under the employment contract. From it you withhold OPV, 10%, and health insurance contributions (VOSMS), 2%, then IPN, 10% of income after deductions. The rest is paid out. Separately, at its own expense, the IP accrues OPVR, 3.5%; social contributions (SO), 5% of salary minus OPV; and health insurance deductions (OOSMS), 3%. There’s no social tax on the simplified regime (KGD clarification).

IPN and deductions

In this lesson’s examples, IPN is figured as under the 2025 rules: OPV, VOSMS, and the basic deduction come off the accrued salary, and 10% is charged on the rest. Whether the new Tax Code kept this order and how large the basic deduction is in 2026, we didn’t verify against the code text — confirm with the KGD. That’s why you set the deduction yourself in the lesson calculator. It doesn’t affect the employee’s cost: the deduction changes only IPN and take-home pay, not the IP’s payments on top.
Per the Kaspi Guide, the IPN rate is 15% on an employee’s annual income above 8,500 MCI (₸36,762,500 in 2026). That’s rare for a shop: on average, more than ₸3,000,000 a month.
Base limits
OPVR and SO are figured on at least 1× minimum wage, ₸85,000.
SO: on at most 7× minimum wage (₸595,000), so no more than ₸29,750 a month.
VOSMS: on at most 20× minimum wage (₸1,700,000), so no more than ₸34,000.
OOSMS: on at most 40× minimum wage (₸3,400,000), so no more than ₸102,000.
OPV and OPVR: on at most 50× minimum wage (₸4,250,000); OPV tops out at ₸425,000, OPVR at ₸148,750.

Payroll sheet and deadlines

It’s handy to keep a payroll sheet for each month: per employee — accrued, OPV, VOSMS, IPN, take-home, OPVR, SO, OOSMS — and totals for each payment at the bottom. You pay the totals no later than the 25th of the next month, and once a quarter you fill in Form 200.00 (lesson 13). The IP’s payments “for yourself” aren’t on the employee sheet; they’re in Form 910.00. Pay “in an envelope” isn’t a saving, it’s a risk. On money paid outside the payroll sheet, no IPN or contributions were withheld and the IP’s payments weren’t charged: an audit can assess them with late-payment interest, and the employee gets no pension contributions on that part. Pay the full salary on the books — the lab below shows how much piles up in a year.

Form 200.00

While an IP has no employees, its report is Form 910.00 for the half-year. Once you hire a mechanic or sign a civil-law (GPH) contract with an individual, the quarterly Form 200.00 is added. How to hire an employee and what one costs is in lesson 12. Here it’s about the books: where the Form 200.00 amounts come from and how to check and file them. The form is shown as a teaching mockup — roughly like this; check the 2026 form’s lines in your account.
Who files and when

Form 200.00 is filed if you have employees or civil-law (GPH) contracts with individuals; without them, it isn’t filed (Tax Code Art. 114(4), per pro1c.kz). The deadline is the 15th of the second month after the quarter: May 15, Aug 15, Nov 15, 2026, and Feb 15, 2027 for Q4. Payroll payments come earlier — every month by the 25th. The IP’s payments for themselves don’t go here: per the portals, they go on Form 910.00 (lesson 6).

This course is for auto electricians and small repair shop owners: how to open a sole proprietorship (IP), choose a tax regime, take payments, hire an employee, and close the IP if needed. Let’s start with choosing a business form. You can work officially as an IP, as an LLP (TOO), or, for some kinds of work, under the self-employed regime. For car repair, the real choice is only between an IP and an LLP; here’s why.
A new Tax Code since 2026

A new Tax Code (No. 214-VIII of July 18, 2025) has been in force since January 1, 2026. There are now three special tax regimes: for the self-employed, the simplified declaration regime (Form 910.00), and one for peasant and farm households. The patent, the retail tax, and the fixed-deduction regime are gone. If you worked under a patent and didn’t file a regime notice by March 1, 2026, check your status: per the State Revenue Committee (KGD), such IPs were deregistered automatically as of January 1, 2026. More in the lesson on changing your regime.

Car repair isn’t possible under the self-employed regime, so the choice is between an IP and an LLP.
The self-employed regime doesn’t cover car repair

Per the State Revenue Committee (KGD), the self-employed regime is for individuals who aren’t registered as an IP (citizens of Kazakhstan and kandas), have no employees, and work only in activities from the Government list (Resolution No. 994 of November 21, 2025). Individual income tax under this regime is 0%, and social payments are 4% of income. There is also a monthly income limit; sources still state it differently, so confirm it with the KGD.

The list has 40 codes: computer repair (95110), consumer electronics and household appliance repair (95210, 95220), taxi (49320), and others. Motor vehicle repair (45.20), auto electrical work, tire service, and car washes aren’t on it, according to the copy of the list published by Halyk Bank; check the official text on adilet.zan.kz. Bottom line: auto electricians and repair shops work as an IP or an LLP.
An IP is the main form for a mechanic and a small shop
An individual registers an IP in their own name. Per public sources, one person can have only one IP.
Registration is by notice, with no stack of documents; how to do it is in the next lesson.
You can hire employees, and since 2026 the simplified regime has no cap on their number (KGD clarification).

On the simplified regime, an IP may skip full accounting and financial statements while annual income stays at or under 135,000 MCI (₸583,875,000 in 2026), and the IP isn’t a VAT payer or a natural monopoly. Source documents and tax records are still required.
When to consider an LLP

An LLP (TOO) is a legal entity with partners and shares. It makes sense when several partners open a shop together and each needs a share in the business. Liability differs too: under the general rule of the Civil Code, an IP is liable for debts with personal property, while an LLP partner risks only their contribution; ask a lawyer for details. Both IPs and LLPs can use the simplified regime, but LLPs face limits: for example, it’s not available if other legal entities own more than 25% of the LLP (KGD clarification).

Working unregistered is a risk

Taking money for repairs without an IP isn’t saving money; it’s a risk. Per public sources (mybuh.kz, 2026), doing business unregistered draws a fine under Article 463 of the Administrative Offenses Code of 15 to 100 MCI (₸64,875 to ₸432,500 in 2026), possibly with confiscation. Since 2026, banks report transfers to individuals’ cards to the KGD when they look like business income, and then come back taxes, late-payment interest, and a fine. So taking repair payments to a personal card isn’t a way to work; it’s a risk.

To open an IP you need two things: an electronic digital signature (EDS) and a notice of starting business. Let’s start with the signature: without it you can’t sign the notice on eGov or applications and tax returns in the taxpayer account. Which activity code to put in the notice is covered in the next lesson, on OKED codes.
Where to get a digital signature

An EDS is your signature for electronic documents: a key and its password. It’s issued online at pki.gov.kz or at a Public Service Center (TsON). The Kaspi.kz app uses its own signature for government services, the Kaspi EDS.

How to protect your signature
Your EDS is yours alone. Anything signed with it is done in your name: notices, applications, tax returns.
Don’t give the key and password to acquaintances or “helpers.” If the key ends up with someone else, reissue your EDS right away on pki.gov.kz or at a TsON.
An EDS has an expiration date, shown in the certificate. Reissue it in advance so you’re not left without a signature when a tax return is due.
If you change your last name, reissue the EDS; your IIN stays the same (per public sources).
Who can become an IP

Per public sources (Kapital.kz, mybuh.kz): a citizen of Kazakhstan can register an IP from age 18, or from 16 with consent of parents or guardians; a foreigner can with a residence permit. It’s not allowed for people the law bars from business, such as civil servants and military personnel, or for those a court has stripped of this right. One person, one IP.
Where to register

It works by notice: you file a notice of starting business, and the tax authority registers the IP. Per a KGD clarification (2023, before the new code), this takes one business day, and no other documents may be demanded; confirm the deadline under the 2026 code with your tax office. Per public sources, registration is free. The options, per mybuh.kz and Kaspi Guide (2026):
eGov.kz or eLicense.kz: the “Notice of starting business as an individual entrepreneur” service, signed with an EDS.
E-Salyq Business, the KGD app: register an IP and choose a special tax regime, then issue receipts, track income, and file Form 910.00.
Kaspi.kz: the “Government Services” section, signed with the Kaspi EDS; you can register an IP only for yourself.
Halyk Onlinebank: the “Stat IP” (Become an IP) service registers you together with a bank account.

OKED is the General Classifier of Economic Activities: every kind of work has its own code. You put the code in your notice when registering the IP, and it shows whether you may use the simplified regime: the list of activities banned from it (Government Resolution No. 970 of November 14, 2025) is built on OKED codes. So a wrong code is not a mere formality.
How to read a code

Read the code left to right, from general to specific. 45 is the section: trade in vehicles and parts, and their repair. 45.20 is motor vehicle maintenance and repair. The fifth digit is the subclass: 45201 or 45202. The full classifier (OKED NK RK 03-2019) is on stat.gov.kz: Reference Books → Classifiers → OKED.
How to read an OKED code
45, section: trade in vehicles and parts, and repair
45.20: motor vehicle maintenance and repair
45201: a shop not in a roadside zone
45202: the same, but a station in a roadside zone
Each next digit narrows the kind of work, from Section 45 down to subclass 45201.
The code for an auto electrician and a shop
45201: maintenance and repair of motor vehicles, except shops in a roadside zone. The main code for a shop or an auto electrician in town.
45202: the same for service stations in the roadside zone of national, regional, and local roads.

Per the classifier’s description, this covers mechanical repair, repair of electrical equipment and electronic fuel injection, body work, washing, painting, glass, and tires. Auto electrical work is “repair of electrical equipment.”
The codes and names here come from OKED reference guides based on stat.gov.kz (version of July 1, 2026). Before registering, check the exact wording on stat.gov.kz.
Selling parts? You need a second code

If you don’t just repair but also sell parts to customers, that’s trade, a separate activity. Add code 45.32, retail sale of auto parts; wholesale is 45.31. Pick the five-digit subclass in the classifier on stat.gov.kz. This doesn’t cost you the simplified regime: Section 45 codes aren’t on list No. 970.

Retail sale of motor fuel: codes 47301 and 47303.
Wholesale of fuel: 46711–46719; wholesale of scrap metal: 46771.
Leasing of cars and trucks: 77112 and 77122; manufacturing of motor vehicles: 29101.
Motor oil and other lubricants fall under group 47.30 in the classifier, not Section 45. Code 47302 isn’t on list No. 970, but 47301 and 47303 are, so pick the code carefully.

Your tax regime determines which tax you pay, what amount it’s calculated on, and which return you file. As covered in lesson 1, the patent is gone as of 2026, and the self-employed regime doesn’t cover car repair. A sole proprietor with a repair bay has two choices: the special tax regime based on a simplified declaration (the “simplified regime”) or the general regime (OUR).
Simplified regime: who qualifies

Per the KGD, the simplified regime is open to IPs and companies whose income for the calendar year is no more than 600,000 MCI (₸2,595,000,000 in 2026) and whose activity isn’t on banned list No. 970. Car repair (Section 45) isn’t on that list, as covered in lesson 3. Since 2026 there’s no longer a cap on the number of employees.
The rate: 4% and the maslikhat decision

Tax on the simplified regime is 4% of income. Income is all the money you get for work: cash, card, QR, transfers. Spending on parts, rent, and wages doesn’t reduce it (Art. 724 of the Tax Code, per a copy of the code text). The local maslikhat (city council) can change the rate: per accounting websites, lower or raise it by up to 50%, so from 2% to 6%; the KGD clarification talks mainly about lowering it.

For Almaty, accounting websites (pro1c.kz) report a 3% rate for 2026 under city maslikhat decision No. 256 of November 28, 2025; per the same data, Astana also has 3% and Shymkent 2%. We haven’t checked the text of the Almaty decision, so confirm with your local tax office whether it limits any kinds of activity.

The half-year and Form 910.00

The tax period on the simplified regime is a half-year, and the return is Form 910.00. Per the KGD tax calendar for 2026, it’s filed no later than the 15th of the second month after the half-year, and the tax is paid by the 25th of that month: for the first half of 2026, by August 15 and 25; for the second half, by February 15 and 25, 2027. There’s no social tax or VAT on the simplified regime. Payments for yourself are separate and monthly; they’re the next lesson.
The general regime (OUR)

On OUR, an IP pays 10% individual income tax (IPN) on income up to 230,000 MCI a year and 15% on the amount above that (Art. 363(4) of the Tax Code, KGD clarification). Expenses are deductible here, which is why a customer on OUR, such as a fleet, cares about your regime: it can’t deduct expenses bought from a simplified-regime IP (Art. 286(16) of the Tax Code). OUR also has a 6% social tax; ask your local tax office how an IP calculates it for themselves. An IP on OUR files Form 220.00.

VAT: the 10,000 MCI threshold

Since 2026 the VAT rate is 16%, and the mandatory registration threshold is 10,000 MCI (₸43,250,000 of annual turnover in 2026). On the simplified regime you don’t register for VAT at any income within the limit, and you can’t register voluntarily (Art. 99 of the Tax Code). On OUR, per a KGD statement, once you pass the threshold you apply for VAT registration within 5 business days. Example: 4 bays × 25 working days × ₸40,000 = ₸4,000,000 a month; on OUR, such a shop passes the threshold in month 11.

Besides the Form 910.00 tax, an IP pays social payments for themselves every month: pension contributions, social contributions, and health insurance contributions. Even if you work alone in your bay with no employees, they’re still yours. The tax is based on half-year income, while these payments are based on declared income, every month.
Four payments
OPV, mandatory pension contributions: 10% of declared income.
OPVR, mandatory employer pension contributions that an IP pays for themselves: 3.5% of declared income in 2026 (it was 2.5% in 2025).
SO, social contributions: 5% of declared income minus OPV; the base is from 1 to 7 minimum wages.
VOSMS, compulsory social health insurance contributions: 5% of 1.4 × the minimum wage, which is ₸5,950 a month at any declared income.

The OPV, OPVR, and VOSMS rates for an IP are per the Kaspi Guide and pro1c.kz (2026). How SO is calculated is per the GFSS (State Social Insurance Fund) clarification of May 14, 2026: the base is income minus OPV. The Social Code doesn’t say this directly, so if in doubt, check with the GFSS or your local tax office.

Declared income: 1 to 50 minimum wages

Declared income is the amount OPV, OPVR, and SO are calculated on. You set it between 1 and 50 minimum wages, which in 2026 is ₸85,000 to ₸4,250,000 a month. That gives each payment a minimum and a maximum: OPV from ₸8,500 to ₸425,000, OPVR from ₸2,975 to ₸148,750, SO from ₸4,250 to ₸29,750 (its base is capped at 7 minimum wages).

A month’s payments are due no later than the 25th of the following month: for January, by February 25; for March, by April 25 (KGD tax calendar for 2026). Who can get it
Registered unemployed people, or IPs that have been operating for no more than 3 years.

Customers pay in different ways: cash, card, Kaspi QR, and fleets by transfer to your account. Each method has its own paperwork. This lesson covers what to give the customer, where to take the money, and where people most often slip up. The key point: all money for repairs is IP income, however the customer pays.
The register and the fiscal receipt

According to clarifications in open sources (mybuh.kz, 2025–2026), payments in cash, by card, by QR code (Kaspi Pay and others), and remote payments are cash settlements. They go through a cash register (KKM), and the customer gets a fiscal receipt. The code does exempt some from the KKM, per open sources, for example lawyers, mediators, and private bailiffs, but auto repair shops aren’t among them. Confirm the article number in the new code and the full list of exemptions with the KGD.

A common mistake is QR with no receipt. A Kaspi bank receipt is a transfer confirmation, not a fiscal receipt. Per open sources, a QR payment, even to the IP account, doesn’t remove the need for a fiscal receipt: ring it up on the KKM with payment type “mobile.”
Kaspi Kassa

According to tax officials at a seminar of the Atameken National Chamber of Entrepreneurs (as reported by finratings.kz, date not given): if the Kaspi Kassa feature is turned on in Kaspi Pay, the payment is fiscalized automatically and the customer gets an electronic fiscal receipt, so no separate KKM receipt is needed; without this feature you need a separate online KKM. No official document confirms this, so check with the KGD and your bank that your register actually issues a fiscal receipt.
The IP account and the 1,000 MCI rule

In practice the IP bank account is opened right at registration through a bank, for example Halyk “Stat IP” or Kaspi Pay. Fleets and companies pay into it, and your QR code is linked to it. When all money for work comes into the IP account and goes through the register, it’s easy to reconcile with Form 910.00.

The 1,000 MCI rule. Under Art. 25(9) of the Law “On Payments and Payment Systems” (per mybuh.kz, 2023), settlements over 1,000 MCI in a single deal (over ₸4,325,000 in 2026) must be non-cash between legal entities, between a legal entity and a VAT-registered IP, and between VAT-registered IPs. An IP on the simplified regime doesn’t pay VAT, so, per the same source, its settlements with LLPs and individuals have no such limit. Check with your bank before a large deal.

Payment for repairs to the mechanic’s personal card isn’t a saving, it’s a risk. It’s still IP income: you must report it on Form 910.00 and give the customer a receipt. If that money isn’t on the return, you face additional tax, late-payment interest, and a fine.
One more rule, from the Law “On Consumer Protection” (Art. 8-1): the price when paying by card can’t be higher than when paying cash. One price for any payment method.

A private customer is a driver who pays for the repair themselves. Their repair is documented with a work order and estimate, an act, and a receipt. This paperwork serves both sides: the customer sees what they’re paying for, and you have proof the work was agreed and accepted. These are also your IP’s source documents (details in the “IP bookkeeping” course).
A work order is the contract for a specific repair: what you’ll do, with what, and for how much. It helps to include:
the customer: name and phone;
the car: make, license plate, mileage;
the customer’s complaint, in their words;
work and parts with prices (your parts or the customer’s); the total is the estimate;
the deadline and warranty terms;
signatures of the customer and the mechanic.

Estimate and extra work

Under Art. 36 of the Law “On Consumer Protection,” an estimate is required if the customer or the contractor insists on one. Extra work beyond the estimate isn’t paid for without the customer’s approval. If it’s clear the estimate will be exceeded, you must warn the customer right away. The law text here and below is from the prg.kz database; check the current wording of the articles on adilet.zan.kz.

Found another fault during the repair? Stop and call the customer before starting that work. Write on the work order what they approved and for how much. Without approval, the customer has the right not to pay for work beyond the estimate.
Act and receipt

When the work is done, the customer accepts it and signs a certificate of completed work (act): what was done and what it costs. The act is an IP source document. Run the payment through the register and give a fiscal receipt (lesson 7). A private customer who paid with a KKM receipt needs no ESF (Art. 208(2) of the Tax Code, per the KGD).
If the customer is unhappy

The customer’s rights when work has a defect are in Art. 35 of the same law. The customer chooses what to demand: fix the defect free of charge, lower the price, redo the work, or reimburse their costs of fixing it.

On the simplified regime tax is figured on income with no deduction for expenses (Article 724 of the Tax Code, per a copy of the code in public sources). Income is everything the customer paid, for labor and for the part. The price you paid the supplier for the part isn’t deducted. Income is adjusted for refunds, discounts, and price changes.

Example: you bought a sensor for ₸20,000, installed it for the customer at ₸24,000, and charged ₸10,000 for labor. Your first hired mechanic is a big step for a shop. Since 2026 the simplified regime has no cap on the number of employees (KGD clarification), but an IP who employs people takes on new duties: the contract and its registration in ESUTD, monthly payroll payments, the quarterly Form 200.00, and workplace safety. Let’s go through them in order.
Employment contract and ESUTD

You sign an employment contract with the employee, and its details go into ESUTD, the Unified Employment Contract Accounting System on Enbek.kz, within 5 working days of signing (Rule 7, Ministry of Labor Order No. 353 of Sept. 3, 2020). Per public sources (mybuh.kz, 2026), since March 2026 late or inaccurate entries draw a fine under Article 98(1-1) of the Administrative Offenses Code: 60 MCI for a small business (₸259,500 in 2026).

Working “off the books” isn’t saving money; it’s a risk. Letting someone work without an employment contract is an offense under the Administrative Offenses Code; sources give the 2026 fine differently, so check with the labor inspectorate. A contract not entered into ESUTD on time draws a separate fine.
